note: Wren Phonics — PSC access arrangements, usable as normal classroom practice without separate STA permission (research §3). provenance: Wren original, b410, 2026-10-08.

arrangements.name: Rest breaks
arrangements.detail: A child may have rest breaks, but the whole check must be finished on the same day. If a child is likely to need breaks more often than between the two sections, STA suggests modifying the materials so there are fewer words on each page.

arrangements.name: Sound buttons — the child marks them, not the adult
arrangements.detail: If a child uses sound buttons in normal classroom practice, they may use them in the check: give the child a clean copy of the check so they can mark the sound buttons themselves. You must not mark the graphemes for the child. Practise this way in Wren Phonics sessions — the child draws the dots and bars.

arrangements.name: Cued Speech and visual phonics
arrangements.detail: Cued Speech may be used by an appropriately trained professional to make a child's responses clear, and visual phonics can be used to make responses clear if this is normal classroom practice.

arrangements.name: Modified materials
arrangements.detail: You may change the font or font size, put fewer words on each page, or use a coloured overlay, if this is normal classroom practice. No permission from STA is needed, but any change must be based on normal classroom practice and must not give the child an advantage.

arrangements.name: What is not allowed
arrangements.detail: Readers are not allowed. Children who use British Sign Language or other sign-supported communication (such as communication boards) to spell out letters, and children who are non-verbal or selectively mute, do not take the check; the headteacher records them as not taking part. Keep teaching and assessing them in the ways described in this guide.

context: Summarised from the Standards and Testing Agency's 2026 Phonics Screening Check administration guidance (section 5.2) and assessment and reporting arrangements. STA updates this guidance every year, so check the current year's version on GOV.UK before the check. Use the same adjustments day to day in phonics sessions, so the check format is never unfamiliar.
